steps.what: List stored till totals for the shift
Count the money in the drawer
Make bank deposits from the counted money

outputs: filed copy of signed deposit count v1

tasks.design: A job lists stored till totals in {ERP}. The manager counts the money and makes the bank deposits. A later job files the signed count in {DOCS}. It does not move the money.
tasks.previous_blocker: Till totals were copied onto a sheet before the count.
tasks.enabler_now: Till identifier and stored total are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The cash is still counted by hand.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week counting, not on listing till totals.

reach.task: Take only the deposit the manager made

evidence.claim: The executive digest says budgets and records come from the booking or ledger system, and a person checks the commentary against the figures.

assumptions: Till identifier, stored total, and shift date are stored on the ledger record. The ledger record produces them. A blank total stays blank and is not treated as zero.
Native configuration of the ledger record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the manager signed is filed or sent.
The file is the signed count. The manager makes the deposit.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining count is still the manager counting the money.

incremental.description: Refresh till identifier and stored total when the ledger layout changes, and drop a count the manager has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many stored totals are blank. The high end assumes till identifier and stored total are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: List service rows with no staff name

outputs: filed copy of signed service standard v1

tasks.design: A job lists service rows in {OPS_SYSTEM} with no staff name. The manager establishes the personnel performance standard and the customer service standard. A later job files the signed standard in {DOCS}. It does not score a named person.
tasks.previous_blocker: Service notes were gathered before each standard was written.
tasks.enabler_now: Service identifier and topic are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The standard is still the manager's judgement.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week on the standard, not on collecting service rows.

evidence.claim: The executive digest says strategy and people work stay manual.
Digest [S9] says a staff decision must not rest on automation alone.
Digest [S10] says hiring, evaluating, or rostering staff on behaviour or traits is high-risk.
Digest [S11] says those duties apply from 2 December 2027.

assumptions: Service identifier, topic, and date are stored on the operations record. The operations record produces them. A blank topic stays blank and is shown as a gap.
Native configuration of the operations record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the manager signed is filed or sent.
The job does not write a score for a named person. A staff decision is not made by the list.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining writing time is still the manager establishing the standard.

incremental.description: Refresh service identifier and topic when the operations layout changes, and drop a standard the manager has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many service topics are blank. The high end assumes service identifier and topic are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Check the record against those rows
Keep the sanitation or subsidy record

outputs: filed copy of signed agency record v1

tasks.design: A job assembles sanitation and subsidy rows from {ERP}. The manager checks each figure against the row and keeps the record. A later job files the signed record in {DOCS}. It does not send the record to an agency.
tasks.previous_blocker: Figures were rekeyed into a fresh record.
tasks.enabler_now: Record identifier, amount, and date are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The manager still checks the figure.
tasks.human_edge: The manager decides what the record says.
tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week checking the record, not on assembling rows.

evidence.claim: The executive digest says budgets and records come from the booking or ledger system, and a person checks the commentary against the figures.
Digest [S15] says a model-drafted review cited sources that were not real. This design does not draft the commentary.

assumptions: Record identifier, amount, date, and record kind are stored on the ledger record. The ledger record produces them. A blank amount stays blank and is not written as zero.
Native configuration of the ledger record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the manager signed is filed or sent.
Filing is internal. Sending the record to an agency would be a separate signed act.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining check is still the manager checking the rows.

incremental.description: Refresh record identifier, amount, and date when the ledger layout changes, and drop a record the manager has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes many amounts are blank. The high end assumes record identifier, amount, and date are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Propose unnamed slots from stored hour rules
Assign duties and names to those slots
Check the hours against the stored rule

outputs: filed copy of signed staff roster v1

tasks.design: A job proposes unnamed slots in {HCM} from stored working-time rules. It writes no person name. The manager assigns the duties and the names, and checks the hours. A later job files the signed roster in {DOCS}. No model is used. Consent for a named roster is a separate decision.
tasks.previous_blocker: The grid was built by hand before the names were written.
tasks.enabler_now: Slot start, slot end, and the working-time rule are already stored.
tasks.still_hard: The manager still chooses the person.

ambition.what: Sign the roster the week the unnamed slots are proposed.

tasks.altitude: The manager spends the week assigning names, not on drawing the grid.

reach.task: Work only the duty the manager signed

evidence.claim: The executive digest says scheduling is a configured product, and working-time rules are solver constraints. No model.
Digest [S4] describes a vendor shift-planning time. This design does not use that figure as its saving.
Digest [S9] says a staff decision must not rest on automation alone.
Digest [S10] says hiring, evaluating, or rostering staff on behaviour or traits is high-risk.
Digest [S11] says those duties apply from 2 December 2027.
Digest [S12] says rosters and staff monitoring need works-council consent.

assumptions: Slot start, slot end, duty, and headcount are stored as solver outputs from the roster record. The roster record produces the working-time rules. A blank rule is shown as a gap and that slot is not proposed. The solver does not write a person name.
Native configuration of the roster record is used before any custom code.
Only the version the manager signed is filed or sent.
Works-council consent for a roster or for monitoring named staff is a separate decision. This design does not treat that consent as already given, and it does not build a camera score of patrons.
unknowns: Who else must see the signed note.
research_questions: How often the required field is blank.

already_counted.description: Half the remaining assignment time is still the manager assigning the duties.

incremental.description: Refresh slot start, slot end, and working-time rule when the roster layout changes, and drop a roster the manager has not signed.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The low end assumes a working-time rule is blank, so that slot is not proposed. The high end assumes slot start, slot end, and the rule are stored. Upkeep is already taken off the central saving.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: The food service manager spends the week on the floor, the guest, and the signed decision. A stored total, a working-time slot with no name, and filing that decision can move. The manager still counts the cash, tastes the food, and assigns the names.
reach: A cook follows only the assignment the manager signed.
A supplier receives only the order the manager signed.
skills_to_grow: Reject a roster slot that already contains a person name.
Reject a total that does not match the stored rows.
Reject an order that the manager has not signed.
role.ambitious_version: A signed roster or order can be filed the same week, and the manager still owns the floor.
